summary: Recommend approve with caution. The design is small, well scoped and has a test mapped to every risk. The implement stage writes code, so the staged diff needs a look before it is applied. No code exists yet, so I could only review the design and not the diff.
what_will_happen: The implement stage builds a new Spring Boot 3.5.6 (Maven, Java 17 target) URL shortener in a staging copy of runs/url-shortener-short/project. It adds pom.xml (web, validation and test starters only), the app classes (LinkController, LinkService, LinkStore, CodeGenerator, ApiExceptionHandler, a security-headers filter), application.properties, a README, and JUnit/MockMvc tests. The tests are LinkApiTest, ConcurrencyTest, LinkServiceTest and LinkStoreTest. The diff then goes through policy checks and is applied to the project. Nothing is deployed or published. Storage is in-memory, with no database or migration.
risks: Open redirect and phishing abuse are inherent to a public shortener. Only scheme and host validation is done, and there is no blocklist or SSRF filtering.
The in-memory map is unbounded and the service has no rate limiting, so memory exhaustion is possible if it is exposed. The design assumes it is not public.
All data is lost on restart. Only the README documents this.
Hand-written URL and alias validation is the main place for bugs: CRLF or control characters, userinfo, case-insensitive schemes, and reserved aliases shadowing /{code}.
Java 17 bytecode built on JDK 25, with an offline Boot 3.5.6 dependency in ~/.m2. The build may fail on a clean machine without network access.

The diff may touch files outside the project, such as the orchestrator working tree. The working tree already has many uncommitted changes and deletions, so confirm the diff is confined to the run's project directory.
The tests may pass without proving the behaviour, for example weak assertions on the 409 and 404 branches or on click counts.
Logging could leak URLs. R14 requires that URLs and bodies are not logged at INFO.
checks_to_perform: Confirm every path in the diff is under C:\Users\pavan\Documents\repos\urlShortner\urlShortner\runs\url-shortener-short\project/ and nothing in orchestrator/, schemas/ or the repo root is touched.
Read pom.xml: parent is spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.6, java.version is 17, and only the web, validation and test starters are present, with no extra or unpinned dependencies (R13).

Read LinkService: URL rules (http/https only, host required, max 2048 characters, no whitespace, control characters or userinfo) and alias regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$ with reserved names rejected. Confirm the alias check uses a full match.
Read LinkStore and LinkService: confirm putIfAbsent is used for both aliases and generated codes. Confirm retries are bounded at 10, return 503, and never overwrite an existing link.
Read LinkController: GET /{code} returns 302 with a single Location header and Cache-Control: no-store. Stats reads must not increment the click count.
Check that shortUrl is built from the app.base-url property and not from the Host or X-Forwarded-Host headers (R11).
Read ApiExceptionHandler: it maps errors to 422, 400, 404 and 409, and error bodies contain no exception class names or stack traces.
Check application.properties and the logging code: request size caps are set and URLs are not logged at INFO (R7, R14).
Run `mvn -B -q test` in the staging copy. Confirm it exits 0 and that the concurrency tests (50-thread alias race, 1000 clicks) really assert exact counts.
Check that every risk R1-R14 and acceptance scenario S1-S7 has an asserting test, and that the README documents the run and test commands and the ephemeral-storage and open-redirect warnings.
Check that no secrets, target/ directories or IDE files are in the diff.
